description: We are a team part of a engineering club located at Fairview High School, Boulder, Colorado.
summary: Terravex consolidates multiple disparate satellite, sensor-based and reanalysis datasets onto a 3D interactive globe and associated epistemic Knowledge Graph, enabling the identification of true climatic change beyond normal intra-annual variability. Using a tech stack of Next.js, TS, Three.js, Python and Postgres, we aggregate data from NASA (EOSDIS/GIBS), POWER, NOAA, USGS and Open-Meteo. This allows us to conduct a suite of distribution-free change detection methods, as well as leverage our novel deep-learning based Trend Microscope and world-wide Spatiotemporal GNN. Applying these techniques to enable overnight pre-charge of storage on a school district's rooftop PV system in Denver, we can identify 88.6% of reduced generation events and save c.$418pa, while considering various uncertainties including lag, FDR and local geospatial conditions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Petabytes of data are gathered each day from space-based and terrestrial sensors. Distinguishing interannual signal is challenging because it is distributed between multiple organizations, masked by strong intrayear periodicity, and often counteracted by other continents. Terravex brings all of these disparate sources together and allows the user to view global raw data on a 5K earth, identify physically linked (teleconnected) phenomena spanning multiple continents using our ETG, and make data-driven decisions about their immediate solar microgrid.

1. Observe: 3D Earth Observatory and Bounded Telemetry After landing on our bespoke Three.js WebGL 5K and 2.5K globe, centered on the astronomical day-terminator line, users can scrub through time and examine 9 NASA EOSDIS and GIBS datasets. Selecting a location will also perform a concurrent (approx 1.6s) query against NASA POWER, USGS National Water Information System (US-only river basins) and Open-Meteo (current NWP, ERA5-derived GloFAS v4, CAMS PM2.5). This is augmented by ongoing searches of NASA GISTEMP v4, EONET v3, NOAA GML, NSIDC, CDO, CSA Geo.ca and KNMI. All returned data is subjected to a suite of autocorrelation-aware statistical analyses: Hamed-Rao and Hirsch-Slack MMK, Theil-Sen with 95% confidence interval, and Pettitt's, corrected for false discovery rate (BH method < 0.05), displayed in original and deseasonalized form.

2. Connect: ETG and "Microscope" NN These confirmed data streams are then linked together via a flat and 3D Knowledge Graph, populated using 4 classes of Ontology (Concept, Signal, Insight, Rule) and continually updated as further corroborating or refuting data emerges. Notably, the ETG makes readily apparent large-scale dipolar events e.g. concurrent increases in Indo-Pacific ENSO Warm Pool SST and decreases in plant EVPTRNS in Madagascar (r=-0.65, p=3.4e-5). Our Microscope NN (etg-trend-microscope-v1) is able to flag incipient anomalies with an AUROC of 0.9789 compared to a rolling-window MMK slope of 0.4442, and predict lead-lag relationships with an AUROC of 0.9916 vs. magnitude of Pearson correlation of 0.7010, eliminating ~98.9% of coincidental relationships.

3. Act: Downstream Microgrid Optimization As a proof-of-concept for downstream use of the global ETG, we simulated an optimal charge level (at 23:00 MDT) overnight for the following day for a hypothetical 250kWdc rooftop solar PV array with 350kWh LiFePO4 storage at a Denver public high-school, given expected reduced solar input that day (< 3.5 kWh m-2 day-1). By accounting for the ~3-5 day near-real-time delay inherent in the POWER product, supplementing with Open-Meteo NWP and monitoring the preceding 5h (18:00-23:00 MDT) advected conditions along a 7-node ETG across the Denver metro Front Range, we obtained a 0.9278 kWh m-2 day-1 RMSE across a 606-day out-of-sample period (2025-26). Compared to Persistence, this represents a 32.9% improvement, correctly identified 88.6% of 'low solar' days and yielded ~$418 per year in avoided billings under CO Time-of-Use tariff structure, roughly 2x that of our app-only Ridge Regressor and direct calculation of P(ALLSKY<3.5). Generalizing this approach using our 2.04M param Spatio-Temporal GNN (etg-global-gnn-v3) trained on 252 POWER locations (36 global cities), we achieved a 22.8% reduction in zero-shot RMSE averaged across 5 held-out geographies spanning 5 continents, with <14ms fp16 execution on a standard desktop CPU.

Benefits & Intended Use Case

Democratized understanding of climate signals, accessible to students through to academic researchers. By clicking anywhere on the 5K globe, the user will see the original and seasonally-debiased data stream, along with associated significance metrics and ?-described Variables. Identification and exploitation of key global-to-local teleconnections to optimize e.g. the 7 upstream nodes feeding their battery.

Integration of external agents: 16 x OpenAPI 3.1.0 MCP functions available at /api/mcp, upload of user-provided data (e.g. Giovanni, AppEEARS, KNMI, Geo.ca) and subscription to live data feeds such as NWS station METARs and third-party IoT (scripts/stream_ground_sensor.mjs).

Development Environment

The codebase is built in TypeScript, Python and SQL, with additional in-house GLSL implementations for simulating and visualizing the effects of Rayleigh and Mie scattering due to orbital position, atmospheric water vapour and clouds. The stack comprises Next.js 16, React 19, Three.js 0.184, Tailwind CSS v4, KaTeX and Zod. Unit and integration testing are performed with Vitest (jsdom) and a range of 'adversarial' inputs, with the platform deployed to Vercel and Railway/Docker.

ML stack: PyTorch (student-teacher distillation in bf16 precision), scikit-learn (quantile HistGradientBoostingRegressor, Ridge), numpy, pandas, matplotlib and native fp16 TS. Model developed over 54,570 days of ETG using Google Colab (NVIDIA A100s) and distilled to ~4MB fp16 model allowing <20ms execution in-browser or via Serverless. Underlying data provided by NASA EOSDIS (GIBS WMTS, WMS), POWER (MERRA-2, CERES), GISTEMP v4, EONET v3, NOAA (GML, NSIDC, CDO), USGS (NWIS), Open-Meteo (NWP, ERA5, GloFAS v4, CAMS) and CSA Geo.ca and KNMI.

Novelty

The ETG is tightly integrated with the 5K Earth and facilitates exploration of drives_opposite and the date at which an existing Insight becomes superseded. Our combination of Hamed-Rao and Hirsch-Slack MMK and Microscope NN is designed to filter out known anti-correlated Northern-Southern hemisphere patterns, quasi-4-quarter-cycle ENSO effects and data errors. We avoid including a fixed buffer to account for the frequency of satellite swaths, instead exploiting the timing of evening upwind advection to align with local TOU billing.

Design Decisions

Strictly maintained forward-only train-val-test partitions (2019-23, 2024, 2025-26 respectively), included autocorrelation correction to derive effective sample size, applied BH-FDR, noted limitations re: pricing and conducted detailed failure mode review (e.g. 2025-05-06). Implemented robust error handling and maximum time limits for each individual telemetry leg, preferred IPv4 and defined chained alternatives (e.g. if USGS unavailable -> GloFAS -> NASA GWETROOT), with informative warnings to the user if the principal source(s) fall behind. Ensured appropriate level of technical depth while remaining user-friendly, incorporating fully-accessible popups and data frames, support for Obsidian dark and high-contrast warm ivory, and concise landing pages to jump-start exploration.
